newsitem.title: UK: BAA down after 40 mln stg interest charge.
newsitem.headline: BAA down after 40 mln stg interest charge.

text.p: Shares in British airports operator BAA Plc were marked down in pre-market trading after it announced an exceptional 40 million stg interest charge for the financial year just ended, dealers said.
BAA shares were down 8.5 pence, or 1.60 percent, to 523.5p by 0715 GMT in volume of 30,000.

BAA said delays in winning planning permission for its 1.5 billion stg project to build a fifth terminal at London Heathrow airport has forced the company to stop capitalising interest on preparatory expenditure.

As a result the company said it would be taking a 40 million stg exceptional interest charge in its results for the year to end-March 1997 to write off the accumulated interest previously capitalised.
BAA said it would also be increasing its interest charges for the year by 13 million stg to take account of the costs for the year just ended.
BAA spiked to a 12-month high just above 550p on Thursday after announcing it had agreed that British Airways Plc and its alliance partners would occupy London's Heathrow giant fifth terminal.
